text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opening of workshop on developing environmental youth leadership in Middle East.
- Islamic Action Front's (Islamist opposition) Shura council calls on regional states to face American "aggression" in Iraq.
- Turkish Foreign Minister Ciller to visit Jordan on Tuesday.
- Jordan's minister of state for foreign affairs arrives in Cairo to attend Arab foreign ministers' meeting.
- Head of U.S.-Arab institute says economic climate in Jordan has encouraged U.S. businessmen to invest there.
- Seizure of 15,000 cartons of smuggled cigarettes.
- Sixteen million dinars ($22.5 million) cost of infrastructure projects in Dead Sea to develop tourism.
- Jordanian-British cooperation in coming Middle East economic summit in Cairo.
- Housing Corporation says plans under way for partnership with private sector in housing projects by end of year.
- Supply minister says lifting import controls by state on private sector commodities purchases will help stabilise prices.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says Jordan is pained by Iraq events but cannot interfere.
- Prime minister said to pledge to consult king on closing file on unrest over bread price increase.
- Kabariti ready to invite Islamists into cabinet, split emerges in Islamist Action Front.
- Amman police seek clues to baffling death of two children.
